language.script: Hangul (phonetic alphabet); Hanja (Chinese characters) occasionally appears in formal/historical contexts but is rare in everyday signage

terrainDescription.zh: 地形多山（約七成為山地丘陵），西部與南部有較多平原與海岸都市帶
terrainDescription.en: Predominantly mountainous (roughly 70% hills/mountains), with more plains and coastal urban development in the west and south

plate.color: black text on white (front & rear); serial format e.g. "12A 3456"

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Yellow flexible posts common in urban areas; rural bollards often carry circular yellow/white reflectors

utilityPole.transformerMount: Distinctive sharp spike-like tip extending above the pole top; diagonal yellow-and-black stripes partway up the shaft (not reaching the ground)

historicalContext.zh: 1443年世宗大王頒布諺文（韓文字母），以取代原本借用的漢字書寫系統；現代韓文街景幾乎完全使用諺文，漢字僅偶爾出現於正式場合。
historicalContext.en: King Sejong promulgated Hangul in 1443 to replace the borrowed Chinese-character writing system; modern street signage is almost entirely Hangul, with Hanja appearing only occasionally in formal contexts.
